title: EGY-08 · At the restaurant and bar: ʿāyiz, lāzim, mumkin

blocks.text: EGY-08 · At the restaurant and bar: ʿāyiz, lāzim, mumkin
Lesson overview

Eating and drinking are the heart of Egyptian social life: it is ordered, tasted, commented, and in the end it is litigated to pay the bill. In this unity learn the three words that hold the daily conversation: ʿāyiz "I want to', lāzim "We need to, we need to, we need to, we can, I can, with their denials" (miš ʿāyiz, miš lāzim, but- yinfaʿš) and with nifsis I want to be. You also learn how to order at the restaurant and coffee, ask for coffee as you want (sāda, mazbūṭ, ziyāda) and to know the most common Egyptian dishes. Six weeks, in parallel with B1-20, the Test B1.3 and B1-21.

rows: 8–9 hours · six weeks (weeks 137–142), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian conversation partner; optional: the menu of an Egyptian restaurant (also online)
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. express wishes with ʿāyiz and nifsis, to the present and past (kunt ʿāyiz);
2. to express needs with lāzim and lack of need with miš lāzim, without confusing it with the ban;
3. ask and give permission with mumkin, yinfaʿ, ma-yinfaʿš;
4. order at the restaurant and coffee, with special requests (no onion, little sugar), and pay;
5. recognize the most common Egyptian dishes and drinks.
Six-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).

3. ʿāyiz and nifsis
ʿāyiz It's a participle. He agrees with whom he wants.
iḥna, intu, humma ʿayzīn miš ʿayzīn kunna ʿayzīn · kānu ʿayzīn

Examples: ana ʿāyiz ʾahwa I'd like a coffee. ʿayza tirūḥ "Want to go" · "kunt" ʿāyiz asʾalak I wanted to ask you, please (as the Italian "volevo"). With a pronoun: ʿayzu I want it. ʿayzha I want it. ʿayzak He wants you, he's looking for you. il-mudīr ʿayzak The director is looking for you. nifsi (Lett. "My soul" expresses a strong desire, often of food or something missing: nifsis ākul maḥši I have a desire to maḥšiNifsis asāfir - I'm dreaming of travelling. It combines with the suffixes: nifsak, nifsik, nifsu, nifsaha, nifsina, nifsukum, nifsuhum.
4. lāzim and miš lāzim

lāzim + imperfect = "needs, must, must: lāzim tigarrab ... you have to try it. lāzim nimši dilwaʾti We have to go now. miš lāzim = - is not necessary, no need miš lāzim tidfaʿ You don't have to pay for it. Warning: it does not mean "not" in the sense of prohibition. The negative imperative is used to prohibit (ma-tidfaʿš! Don't pay!06) o ma-yinfaʿš It is not possible to do so. lāzim for a deduction: lāzim huwwa taʿbān It must be tired (as the Italian must be.....)
5. mumkin and yinfaʿ
mumkin + imperfect: courteous request and permission.

rows: Could you pass me the salt?

blocks.text: mumkin bukra Maybe tomorrow

mumkin by itself also means "maybe": "mumkin" āgi, mumkin laʾ Maybe I'll come, maybe I won't. yinfaʿ / ma-yinfaʿš It's okay, it's possible / you can't do it: yinfaʿ adfaʿ Bi-l-kart? — laʾ, ma-yinfaʿš, kāš Bass "No, you can't, just cash" yinfaʿ asks whether something is acceptable or feasible.

9. Pronunciation

ʿāyiz, ʿayza, ʿayzīn. The ʿ initial is always heard; in female and plural ā shortens: ʿāyiz but ʿayza, ʿayzīn. Practice with the tutor: ʿāyiz šāy / ʿayza ʾahwa / ʿayzīn ʿaṣīr. The ʾ Egyptian. ʾahwa Caffès (caffès), ʾaṣab "Cannae" is the name of the species, ʾayma • • • • • • • fuṣḥā has ⁧ق⁩ ( ⁧قَهْوَة⁩ , ⁧قَصَب⁩ , ⁧قَائِمَة⁩ ), Cairo has a glottis stroke. In Egyptian writing remains the ⁧ق⁩ . Rhythm of the request. mumkin il-ḥisāb, law samaḥt? with the tone that goes up at the end: it is the kind request. That dish sounds like an order.

1. At the restaurant (session). Roleplay with the tutor in the role of the waiter: come in, ask for a table, ask

3. What do you like? Tell the tutor what you'd like to eat in Cairo (nifsis...), what you need
